# K5.1 Sliding-window attention with sinks (Triton)

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Class: **Same function** (E1: same function at infinite precision, different floating-point
order)

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

- `NVFP4_SWA_TRITON=1` (config line 144). Same value in G3,
  G6, G6b and G6c.
- Code: `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/basic/nvfp4_swa_attention.py`, created by
  `docker/patches/transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` L241–807 (the patch is byte-identical in the three
  implementation directories), installed by the `NVFP4_SWA_TRITON` block of `pretrain.py`
  (in G3, G6 and G6b; see below for G6c).
- **G6c:** the same switch installs `firmus_kernels/swa_attention.py` instead (`pretrain.py` L128–133). That file is
  the TE-patch module of this write-up with a compile-time `HAS_SINK`; this model's softmax is vanilla (no sink,
  `conf/gpt_oss.yaml` L36) and its window is (128, 0) (`sliding_window_keys` 129, L35; `pretrain.py` L1099), so the
  sink-free specialisation runs. That path and `NVFP4_SWA_PDKDV` (set in G6c only) are described in K10.2. Sections
  2–7 below describe the kernel with sinks, which is in the image (TE patch) but not called in G6c; the same code is
  the `HAS_SINK=True` specialisation of the G6c file.
- The tuning variables `NVFP4_SWA_FWD`, `_DKDV`, `_DQ`, `_PFWD`, `_PDKDV`, `_PDQ`, `_PACKED` and
  `NVFP4_FULL_ATTN_FP8` are not set in the config; their defaults are at patch L272–275 and L763.
- Full-attention layers are not touched by this item:
  they run cuDNN FP8 attention (K8.1).

## 2. What the reference does

Megatron's `TEDotProductAttention` (TE `27486e03`) with the model settings of G6b's `pretrain.py`
(L1035–1038, L1045, L1065–1066; the earlier model, not this package's file):
64 query heads, 8 KV groups, head dim 64, attention dropout 0, `window_size=(127, 0)`,
`softmax_type="learnable"`. For the window layers TE runs cuDNN fused attention: query \(i\) attends keys
\(i-127 \ldots i\), and the per-head sink \(z_h\) (`softmax_offset`) is an extra softmax logit with no value:

\[ p_{ij} = \frac{ e^{s_{ij} } }{ e^{z_h} + \sum_{k} e^{s_{ik} } },\qquad o_i = \sum_j p_{ij} v_j . \]

The upstream TE and cuDNN source is not in the package; it is not cited by line here.

## 3. What this implementation does

1. `install()` (patch L755–807) wraps `TEDotProductAttention.forward`. Eligible calls (Section 6) go to
   `swa_attention(query, key, value, self.softmax_offset, self.fused_attention.softmax_scale, window[0])`
   (L795–797); every other call goes to the original forward (L805–806).
2. Forward, packed kernel `_swa_fwd_packed` (L468–520): one tile holds 4 query heads of one KV group × 32 query
   rows. The online softmax runs in base 2 and starts from the sink: `m = sink·log2e`, `l = 1` (L491–492). Key
   blocks run from the window start to the row (L497–499), out-of-window logits are set to −inf (L504–505), and
   the row's log-sum-exp is stored for the backward (L520).
3. Backward: `delta_i = Σ o_i·do_i` (`_swa_bwd_pre`, L334–349). `_swa_bwd_dkdv_packed` (L523–577): one program per
   64-key block of one KV group owns its dK and dV and loops over the 8 query heads and the query blocks that see
   it, so no atomics are used. `_swa_bwd_dq_packed` (L580–640) writes dQ and a per-program partial of the sink
   gradient `−Σ_i p_{i,sink}·delta_i` (L636–640); the partials are summed with `torch.sum` (L746).

G6c: the reference is the same TE call with `window_size=(128, 0)` and `softmax_type="vanilla"` (`pretrain.py`
L1099–1100), that is, the formula above without the \(e^{z_h}\) term (K10.2).
## 4. Why the result is the same

Forward and backward evaluate the same masked softmax with sink and its exact gradient (the sink carries no value,
so \(\partial L/\partial z_h = -\sum_i p_{i,\mathrm{sink} }\,\delta_i\)). Only the evaluation order changes: block
sizes, the order of the online-softmax rescaling, `exp2` with the scale folded into `qk_scale = sm_scale·log2e`
(L664), and where P and dS are rounded to BF16 before the matrix products. Class **Same function** (E1).

vs reference / vs FP64 (captured q, k, v and sink of a G6 training run, seven layers, job 22403): relative L2 error vs FP64, TE / Triton, out 1.77e-3–1.97e-3 / 1.69e-3–1.81e-3,
dq 2.40e-3–6.30e-3 / 2.36e-3–6.09e-3, dk 3.00e-3–5.50e-3 / 2.46e-3–5.05e-3, dv 2.76e-3–2.88e-3 /
2.20e-3–2.35e-3, dsink 1.69e-3–2.49e-3 / 1.77e-3–3.91e-3 (Triton higher in dsink on layers 22 and 23). Seeded
real shape, job 22181: out 0.0023 / 0.0021, dq 0.0024 / 0.0024, dk 0.0029 / 0.0024, dv 0.0029 / 0.0023, dsink
0.0022 / 0.0020. Triton vs cuDNN on the real shape: out 47.4 M of 100.7 M elements differ.

## 5. Numerics

BF16 q, k, v; `tl.dot` accumulates in FP32. P is cast to BF16 before P·V (L511) and dS to BF16 before dS·K and
dSᵀ·Q (L569–572, L628). Softmax statistics and LSE are FP32. Outputs BF16; sink gradient FP32 partials, summed,
then cast to the sink dtype (L746). Triton compiles at run time; no compiler options are set.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** patch L774–787: `window_size` set with `window[1] == 0` and `window[0] > 0`, `softmax_type ==
  "learnable"`, causal mask type, no attention bias, no packed-sequence parameters, `qkv_format == "sbhd"`, BF16
  query, head dim 64 or 128. `_check` (L643–652) raises for non-4-D tensors, non-unit last stride, mismatched
  shapes, or query heads not a multiple of KV heads.
- **Falls back:** to the original TE forward (L805–806), silently. Only the Triton path logs, once, on rank 0
  (L788–794). Job 22413: window None, full window, right window 1, vanilla softmax, padding mask, attention bias,
  packed sequence, bshd, FP16 and head dim 96 each give 0 Triton calls and 1 original call.
- **Assumes:** (a) attention dropout is 0: the gate does not test it and the kernel has no dropout; with dropout
  > 0 the dropout would be skipped silently (`attention_dropout=0.0`, `pretrain.py`
  L1084). (b) Heads per KV
  group divisible by the packed tile (4 for forward and dQ, 2 for dK/dV, `PCFG` L274; in G6c 4 for all three, K10.2); only `H % G` is checked. With
  64 heads and 64 groups the test stops with "Triton Error: misaligned address"; training has 8 heads per group.
  (c) No context parallelism: the gate does not test it; with CP > 1 the kernel would attend only to the local
  chunk (`CONTEXT_PARALLEL=1`, config L16). (d) `attention_mask` is not read; causality comes from the mask type.
- **Check:** config line 144; every `result_*.txt` (10 of 10 runs) contains, printed by the
  G6c file (K10.2), `NVFP4 SWA Triton attention window=(128, 0) q=(8192, 3, 64, 64) k=(8192, 3, 8, 64) packed=True
  cfg={'FWD': (4, 32, 32, 4, 3), 'DKDV': (4, 16, 64, 4, 3), 'DQ': (4, 32, 32, 4, 3)}`
  (`result_0.txt` line 1039).

## 7. Code

- `transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` L241–807: kernels L278–640, `SWAAttentionFunc` L655–747, `install`
  L755–807. Applied by `Dockerfile` step 4 (L106–121, `git apply` L113).

## 8. Tests and evidence

- `k5_1_swa` (with sinks) was not run on this image. Firmus test script `k10_2_swa_vanilla.py` (available on
  request), job 22903, runs the G6c file's `HAS_SINK=True` specialisation against this TE-patch kernel on the same
  inputs: with a random sink and with sink −inf, 0 differing elements in out, dq, dk, dv and dsink (K10.2).
- The G6 results of `k5_1_swa` follow, for the TE-patch kernel itself.

- 39 cases, 33 with a difference. 31 are real rounding differences, Triton vs cuDNN: seeded and captured real
  shapes (seven captured layers: 5 of 14 outputs differ, 76–87 M elements), special values, constant rows, sink
  values +20 / 0 / −30, head dim 128, sequence lengths 64, 127, 128, 129, 8191, 8193, packed and unpacked. One is
  the control `control_te_vs_te` (cuDNN vs cuDNN, two calls): dsink differs in 64 of 64 (run a, max 2.1e-5) and
  59 of 64 (run b), so cuDNN's sink gradient is not repeatable. One is the fixture `fixture_window_126` (window off
  by one, 203 M elements, by design).
- Run a vs run b: 302 digests equal, 1 differs (the cuDNN control). Every Triton output is repeatable across
  processes; prefill 0x00 / 0xFF and fresh process: 0 differ (job 22413).
- GQA 64/1 runs (5 outputs differ, rounding). GQA 64/64 stops (Section 6, Assumes b).
- Run log: the Section 6 line in all 10 scored runs of each package.
- Development test `overlays_v4/test_swa_attention.py` (development repository) loads a development copy, not
  the installed module.

## 9. Open points

1. No guard for heads per KV group that are not a multiple of 4; such a model fails at run time instead of
   falling back. Training uses 8.
2. Dropout and context parallelism are not in the gate (Section 6, Assumes a and c).
3. The vs-FP64 numbers are from the G6 image (jobs 22181, 22403); the final jobs 22432 and 22669 record the same
   case set; their vs-FP64 values are not quoted here (not checked for this write-up).
